facts.text: Troy was organized as a township in 1827, and after sections of the township were incorporated into Birmingham, Clawson and Royal Oak, the remainder was incorporated as the City of Troy in 1955.

The roughly three-mile stretch of Big Beaver Road between Rochester Road and Coolidge Highway forms Troy's central business district, one of the busiest corridors in Oakland County, with high-rise office buildings and hotels along the way.
The two buildings of the Somerset Collection, connected by an enclosed pedestrian bridge, flank Big Beaver Road as it approaches Coolidge Highway.
Troy is home to both the Somerset Collection and Oakland Mall.

The Troy Historic Village, at 60 W. Wattles Road on the northwest corner of Wattles and Livernois, is a collection of 11 buildings surrounding a gazebo and green, with the 1927 Township Hall serving as its visitor center.
The year-round ice rink and pavilion at Jeanne M. Stine Community Park, on the city's Civic Center campus at the corner of Civic Center Drive and Town Center Drive, was completed in June 2024.
The City of Troy holds an annual Holiday Tree Lighting Ceremony in early December, which in 2025 moved from Troy City Hall to The Rink at Stine Community Park.
The Lloyd A. Stage Nature Center and Troy Farm share a 100-acre parcel, with nature center trails through meadow, forest, marsh and river areas.
Troy's community parks include Boulan Park on Crooks Road and Firefighters Park on Square Lake Road, where a section of the Rouge River runs through the grounds.

christmas-light-installation.title: Christmas Light Installation in Troy, MI
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Christmas light installation in Troy, MI. Clean roofline runs, wrapped trees and lit shrubs, with in-season service and takedown. Book a free estimate.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Troy, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: Measured roofline runs, wrapped trees and lit shrubs for Troy homes, with the layout planned first and the lights taken down once the holidays pass.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: Troy's business side, with office towers and hotels on Big Beaver Road and two major shopping centers, is only half the city. At home, holiday lighting is about something closer: a house that looks sharp from the street and the driveway every evening, with none of the ladder work falling on you. We start by measuring the rooflines and noting the trees and shrubs worth lighting, then plan the power around your outlets and circuits. Crews install from the ground, the roof and the bucket truck as the house requires, test everything before leaving and return after the holidays to take it down. If your subdivision entrance needs lighting too, it can be planned in the same season.
considerations: A roofline is rarely one straight line. Garages, gables and dormers each change the run, so we measure every section and plan how the lights meet at corners and peaks. The result looks balanced from the street instead of heavy on one side.

A lit roofline alone can look like it is floating. Wrapping a front yard tree and lighting the shrubs along the foundation connects the house to the ground and gives the display depth. We suggest a mix during the estimate, and you choose what fits.

If your subdivision has an association with rules on exterior decorations or display timing, share them with us early. The estimate describes the layout clearly, which makes it simple to confirm the plan fits before installation day.
faq: Do you hang Christmas lights for Troy homes?
Yes, we serve homes across Troy. Send your address through the estimate form or call (248) 756-8915, and we will visit the house, measure the rooflines and put together a free estimate.
When should I book to be lit by early December?

The earlier in the fall you reach out, the more install dates you can choose from. Installs commonly land between October and early December, and Troy's Holiday Tree Lighting Ceremony comes near the end of that window, which makes it a sensible target. Later requests are handled as dates allow.
Do you come back if something stops working?

Yes. In-season service is part of the plan, so if a section goes dark or weather knocks something loose, call us and we will schedule a visit. The crew also comes back after the holidays for takedown, so the roof is clear before spring.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Troy, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Commercial holiday lighting in Troy, MI for offices, hotels, retail centers and HOAs. Entrance displays, tree wraps and building outlines. Free estimate.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Troy, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Entrance displays, tree wraps and building outlines for Troy offices, hotels, retail properties and associations.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: Big Beaver Road, from Rochester Road to Coolidge Highway, is Troy's central business district: roughly three miles of office towers and hotels along a corridor that ranks among Oakland County's busiest. The city is also home to two regional malls. For the offices, hotels and retail properties along the corridor, holiday lighting has to register from a moving car and still look polished at the front door. We focus where people actually look: entrances, drop-off areas, landscaped islands, lower facades and trees along the drive. Bucket-truck crews handle the elevated work, and we schedule around tenants, guests and deliveries. Service continues through the season, and removal follows.
considerations: Tall office buildings are seen from far away, but a holiday display does its work at street and entrance level. The walkthrough sets what is reachable from the bucket truck and puts the lighting where drivers and visitors actually look.

Along a busy corridor, most people see a property from a car. Bold, simple shapes read better at that speed than fine detail: an outlined entrance, wrapped trees along the drive, a lit focal point near the sign. Finer work is saved for the front door.

A hotel entrance never really closes, and retail parking fills quickly in December. We plan lift work and cord runs away from busy entrances where possible and confirm timing with your team before the crew arrives.
faq: Do you offer commercial holiday lighting in Troy?

Yes. Offices, hotels, retail properties, associations and property managers in Troy can book a walkthrough, and the estimate that follows is free. A manager with several sites can bundle them into one plan, with one contact for the whole season.
How early should a Troy business book?

Commercial walkthroughs are easiest in late summer and early fall, before install season fills up. Properties aiming to glow before the heaviest shopping weeks should plan early. If you are reaching out later, call anyway, and we will be straight about what can fit.
What does the commercial estimate include?

A site walkthrough, a design built around how people approach the property, a map of power and lift access, and a written estimate listing each part of the season, from installation and service calls to removal. You pay nothing for the walkthrough or the estimate.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Christmas Lights in Troy, MI
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Permanent Christmas lights in Troy, MI. App-controlled roofline lights for Christmas, graduations and nightly accent lighting, installed once.
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: Roofline lights that stay up all year and change with a tap, from Christmas warm white to game-day colors.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: The rink at Stine Community Park runs year-round, and permanent lighting works on the same idea at home: built once, used in every season. The lights ride in a low-profile track tucked under the eaves, where it stays discreet during the day. From an app you choose colors, scenes and timing, so the lights can run warm white through the holidays, glow softly every evening at dusk or take on school colors for a graduation party. Birthdays and summer cookouts can get their own looks too. We measure the roofline, plan the power, install the track and lights, and walk you through the app before we leave.
considerations: Because permanent lighting is not tied to December, it can go in during a calmer part of the year. Planning it in spring, summer or early fall means the roofline is ready well before the holidays, with nothing left to schedule when installers are busiest.

A permanent outline is only as good as its corners. We plan how the track turns at gables, steps across garage rooflines and wraps around the house, so the lights look continuous after dark and the connections stay tucked away.

If your Troy subdivision has an association, ask whether it reviews permanent exterior fixtures and how long approval tends to take. Knowing that early keeps the install date from slipping while the paperwork catches up.
faq: Is permanent lighting available in Troy, MI?

Yes. Permanent, app-controlled roofline lighting is available in Troy and across Oakland County. Start with a free estimate: we check the roofline, eaves and power, then send a layout and a written estimate of what is included.
What does everyday accent lighting look like?

Usually a soft warm white or a subtle color along the roofline, scheduled to turn on at dusk and off at a set hour. It highlights the architecture, makes the house easier to find at night and needs no attention once the schedule is set.
Do I need to be home for installation?

For part of it, ideally. We need access to the exterior and the power source, and the app setup goes smoothly with you there so we can walk through colors, scenes and schedules together. We set the appointment with you in advance.
